steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: When Hitler became Chancellor in January 1933, over 6 million Germans were unemployed - nearly 30% of the workforce. By 1939, official unemployment was under 500,000. The Nazis claimed to have solved the unemployment crisis, but the reality was more complex. | Key Fact: The Nazis launched massive public works programmes, most famously the autobahn (motorway) network. Between 1933 and 1938, over 3,000 km of autobahn were built. However, the autobahn programme was originally proposed by the Weimar government - the Nazis simply took credit for it. | Key Fact: Rearmament was the single biggest factor in reducing unemployment. Government spending on arms rose from 3.5 billion marks in 1933 to 30 billion marks by 1939. By 1939, 40% of government expenditure was on the military. | Key F

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain two ways the Nazis reduced unemployment. (4 marks) | How important was rearmament in reducing German unemployment? (8 marks) | "Nazi economic policies benefited German workers." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from nazi economic policies, and one past-paper question.
